sentences.en: Hello, everybody.

sentences.en: Welcome back to the show.

sentences.en: Welcome back to the podcaSt.

sentences.en: New listeners, old listeners, wherever you are in the world, it is so great to have you here back for another episode as we, of course, break down the psychology of our 20s.
sentences.zh: 无论你是新听众还是老听众，无论你身处世界何地，很高兴你能回来收听新的一期节目，当然，我们要继续剖析20多岁的心理。

sentences.en: Today, we are talking about something that has become absolutely mega huge.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要谈论一个已经变得非常非常火爆的话题。

sentences.en: I would say in, like, the last year.
sentences.zh: 我想说是在过去一年左右的时间里。

sentences.en: What we are talking about is the rise of run clubs, run mania, half marathon ambitions, people putting their Strava on their hinge profiles,
sentences.zh: 我们要谈论的是跑步俱乐部的兴起、跑步热潮、半程马拉松的雄心壮志，人们把Strava链接放在Hinge个人资料上，

sentences.en: people Saturday mornings booked out to run 3K, 5K, 10K.
sentences.zh: 人们把周六早上的时间都预留出来去跑3公里、5公里、10公里。

sentences.en: Seemingly over the night, running has become, like, the new frontier of fun.
sentences.zh: 仿佛一夜之间，跑步已经成为了乐趣的新前沿。

sentences.en: And I have to admit, I myself have been bit by the running bug.
sentences.zh: 我必须承认，我自己也被跑步这种“病毒”感染了。

sentences.en: And not just, like, the running bug, the run club bug.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是跑步，是“跑步俱乐部”这种病毒。

sentences.en: Here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 事情是这样的。

sentences.en: I distinctly remember.
sentences.zh: 我清楚地记得。

sentences.en: It's a very, it's a core memory.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常核心的记忆。

sentences.en: Core memory for me.
sentences.zh: 对我来说是核心记忆。

sentences.en: I remember saying to one of my best friends last year, if I join a run club, stop me.
sentences.zh: 我记得去年曾对一位好朋友说，如果我加入跑步俱乐部，一定要阻止我。

sentences.en: Something is wrong.
sentences.zh: 那一定是有什么不对劲。

sentences.en: Like, something is wrong.
sentences.zh: 就像是，有什么地方出问题了。

sentences.en: This is not me.
sentences.zh: 这根本不是我。

sentences.en: I've turned down the wrong path.
sentences.zh: 我走上了一条错误的道路。

sentences.en: I have always hated running.
sentences.zh: 我一直都很讨厌跑步。

sentences.en: I would try for a few months, maybe run, like, max, like, 3 kilometers, which is still quite far, and then kind of just give up.
sentences.zh: 我曾经尝试过几个月，也许最多跑个3公里，这已经很远了，然后就放弃了。

sentences.en: And I always was like, you know what, running just isn't for me.
sentences.zh: 我总是觉得，你知道吗，跑步真的不适合我。

sentences.en: I'm just not going to be that kind of gal.
sentences.zh: 我注定不会成为那种女孩。

sentences.en: Like, it's just not in the cards.
sentences.zh: 这根本不在我的计划之内。

sentences.en: Now I'm at a point where I'm running 30 kilometers a week.
sentences.zh: 现在我每周能跑30公里。

sentences.en: I have a running veSt.
sentences.zh: 我甚至有了一件跑步背心。

sentences.en: And every Sunday, without fail, I'm at the park at 8 a.m., ready to do my three laps with my friends.
sentences.zh: 每个周日，雷打不动，我早上8点都会出现在公园，准备和朋友们跑完三圈。

sentences.en: And I keep thinking back to that person, that version of me, who kind of didn't know what she was missing.
sentences.zh: 我不断回想起那个曾经的自己，那个不知道自己错过了什么的女孩。

sentences.en: I love my run club.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的跑步俱乐部。

sentences.en: And this, it turns out, is no accident.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，这一切并非偶然。

sentences.en: I think especially in our 20s and 30s, when loneliness can really creep in quite easily and our identity feels very slippery, there is something quite powerful about showing up
sentences.zh: 我认为特别是在我们20多岁和30多岁的时候，当孤独感很容易悄然而至，而我们的身份认同感又显得非常模糊时，能够坚持做一些如此简单、重复、社交化，且在潜移默化中带来改变的事情，是非常有力量的。

sentences.en: for something so simple, so repetitive, so social, and kind of quietly very transformative.
sentences.zh: （续上句）

sentences.en: You know, you don't need to be faSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你不需要跑得很快。

sentences.en: You don't need to know anyone.
sentences.zh: 你不需要认识任何人。

sentences.en: You just need to keep putting one foot in front of the other.
sentences.zh: 你只需要不断地迈出脚步。

sentences.en: And then at the end, you get rewarded with a really convenient kind of socialization that I don't think a lot of us have experienced
sentences.zh: 最后，你会得到一种非常便捷的社交回报，我认为我们很多人自从高中、大学，或者研究生毕业后，就很少体验过这种感觉了。

sentences.en: since high school or college or maybe like a graduate program.
sentences.zh: （续上句）

sentences.en: Additionally, I think when some of the earliest structures we relied upon to give our life meaning fall away, running is a really positive and easy space to set goals in.
sentences.zh: 此外，我认为当一些我们曾经依赖的、赋予生活意义的早期结构消失时，跑步是一个设定目标的非常积极且简单的空间。

sentences.en: It is very easy if you are capable to see effort directly reflected in performance.
sentences.zh: 如果你有能力，很容易就能看到努力直接反映在表现上。

sentences.en: You know, you run more, you add more kilometers, you train harder, you will see an improvement.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你跑得越多，增加的里程越多，训练越刻苦，你就会看到进步。

sentences.en: Whereas in other areas of our life, progress is a lot harder to track.
sentences.zh: 而在我们生活的其他领域，进步要难追踪得多。

sentences.en: It's not as linear.
sentences.zh: 它不是那么线性的。

sentences.en: And, you know, of course, exercise also just makes us feel good.
sentences.zh: 而且，当然，运动也会让我们感觉良好。

sentences.en: So there's like the inherent reward in that as well.
sentences.zh: 所以这本身也是一种内在的回报。

sentences.en: So in today's episode, we are going to dive into the psychology of run clubs and their emotional pull, especially in our 20s and 30s.
sentences.zh: 所以在今天的节目中，我们将深入探讨跑步俱乐部的心理学及其情感吸引力，特别是在我们20多岁和30多岁的时候。

sentences.en: We're going to talk about their inherent benefits, how they're actually quite positive anchors, and what they reveal about how we want to be seen
sentences.zh: 我们将讨论它们固有的好处，它们如何成为非常积极的锚点，以及它们揭示了我们在这一阶段希望如何被看待、被支持，以及我们希望如何与他人建立联系。

sentences.en: and support and how we want to connect as humans in this decade.
sentences.zh: （续上句）

sentences.en: We're also going to dive into the downsides, downsides that I have seen myself, especially when run clubs are not inclusive or they're too image-based,
sentences.zh: 我们还将深入探讨其负面影响，我自己也见过，特别是当跑步俱乐部不够包容或过于注重形象时，

sentences.en: and how we can continue to engage in them in a way that serves us without feeling let down by these other elements that have no space in this community.
sentences.zh: 以及我们如何能以一种服务于自己的方式继续参与其中，而不被这些在这个社区中毫无立足之地的因素所困扰。

sentences.en: So this one is for all my runners out there, my run-curious listeners, maybe even the movement avoided who are like looking at run clubs thinking that looks awful.
sentences.zh: 所以这一期是献给所有跑步者、对跑步感兴趣的听众，甚至是对运动避之不及、觉得跑步俱乐部看起来糟透了的人们。

sentences.en: Why would anyone want to do that?
sentences.zh: 为什么会有人想做那种事？

sentences.en: Hopefully this episode gives you kind of an idea.
sentences.zh: 希望这一集能给你一些启发。

sentences.en: So without further ado, let's get into the unexpected psychology of run clubs.
sentences.zh: 那么废话不多说，让我们进入跑步俱乐部那意想不到的心理学世界。

sentences.en: So first off, let's answer this very big question.
sentences.zh: 首先，让我们回答这个非常宏大的问题。

sentences.en: Why are run clubs suddenly everywhere?
sentences.zh: 为什么跑步俱乐部突然到处都是？

sentences.en: What has changed in our social fabric that has made the simple act of collectively jogging together such a powerful magnet for community?
sentences.zh: 我们的社会结构发生了什么变化，使得集体慢跑这种简单的行为成为了社区如此强大的磁铁？

sentences.en: It turns out run clubs are basically filling a very crucial void that we have as a generation that very little else is prepared to fill.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，跑步俱乐部基本上填补了我们这一代人非常关键的空白，而其他事物几乎无法填补。

sentences.en: Consider this.
sentences.zh: 考虑一下这一点。

sentences.en: Many of us in our 20s are experiencing what psychologists would call social displacement.
sentences.zh: 我们许多20多岁的人正在经历心理学家所说的“社会流离失所”。

sentences.en: So we are often moving to new cities for jobs.
sentences.zh: 我们经常为了工作搬到新的城市。

sentences.en: We are chasing opportunities far from our hometowns.
sentences.zh: 我们在远离家乡的地方追逐机会。

sentences.en: We graduate from university or we finish school or we finish apprenticeships.
sentences.zh: 我们大学毕业，或者完成了学业，或者完成了学徒期。

sentences.en: And suddenly we kind of lose those built-in effortless structures of friendship.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，我们失去了那些内置的、毫不费力的友谊结构。

sentences.en: You don't have daily class.
sentences.zh: 你不再有每天的课程。

sentences.en: You don't have campus clubs.
sentences.zh: 你不再有校园社团。

sentences.en: You don't have shared dorm rooMs.
sentences.zh: 你不再有共享宿舍。

sentences.en: That constant easy proximity to friends, I feel like it almost vanishes overnight.
sentences.zh: 那种与朋友轻松相处的亲密感，我觉得几乎是一夜之间就消失了。

sentences.en: And you're suddenly spending a lot more time alone when perhaps you don't really want to.
sentences.zh: 你突然开始花更多的时间独处，而这或许并不是你想要的。

sentences.en: You're trying desperately to build new communities in new spaces.
sentences.zh: 你拼命地试图在新的空间里建立新的社区。

sentences.en: And it's really hard.
sentences.zh: 这真的很难。

sentences.en: This is not just you.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是你个人的问题。

sentences.en: This is not an isolated experience.
sentences.zh: 这并非孤立的经历。

sentences.en: There was a 2021 study published in the very famous journal Nature, and it actually analyzed mobile phone data from millions of users.
sentences.zh: 2021年发表在著名期刊《自然》上的一项研究，分析了数百万用户的手机数据。

sentences.en: And it confirmed that our friendship networks do tend to shrink significantly constantly and quite rapidly during our 20s.
sentences.zh: 它证实了我们的友谊网络在20多岁时确实倾向于持续且相当迅速地显著缩小。

sentences.en: This is because we become more selective.
sentences.zh: 这是因为我们变得更加挑剔了。

sentences.en: Also, it's just, you know, convenience, distance, and the fact that the effort required to forge new friendships, it's really overwhelming when you don't have that base level
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，还有便利性、距离，以及这样一个事实：当你没有那种相互了解或相似性的基础时，建立新友谊所需的努力真的让人感到不知所措。

sentences.en: of knowing each other or similarity.
sentences.zh: （续上句）

sentences.en: The best name I have for it is a friendship recession, and it leaves many of us feeling like a very profound sense of loneliness.
sentences.zh: 我能想到的最好的名字是“友谊衰退”，它让我们许多人感到一种非常深刻的孤独感。

sentences.en: Also, despite being really hyper-connected online, spending even more time on our phone, it doesn't really seem to be helping.
sentences.zh: 此外，尽管我们在网上联系极其紧密，花更多的时间在手机上，但这似乎并没有什么帮助。

sentences.en: We actually are more lonely than ever before.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上比以往任何时候都更加孤独。

sentences.en: That irony is like not lost on me.
sentences.zh: 这种讽刺意味我并没有忽略。

sentences.en: You know, we are digitally saturated, but we are relationally starved.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们在数字上是饱和的，但在人际关系上却是匮乏的。

sentences.en: Like, social media has convinced us that we can be more in contact than ever before, but the level of contact is so shallow.
sentences.zh: 社交媒体让我们相信我们可以比以往任何时候都联系得更紧密，但这种联系的程度太浅了。

sentences.en: And that is actually a real growing concern.
sentences.zh: 这实际上是一个真正令人担忧的问题。

sentences.en: You may have heard the statistic that loneliness is as dangerous as smoking a packet of cigarettes a day.
